items.title: Misremembered web_fetch calls?!
items.body: I will just cross-post this here (from https://github.com/blazux/qwen3.8-Flash-DGX/issues/16) since the issue might as well sit inside OpenFox. I'm using your vLLM recipe and altough I suspect this has nothing to do with your contributions, I'm kind of at a loss where to look for testers. The thing is: ALL my web_fetch requests seem to somehow be rewritten inside the LLM itself! I took a pcap on the harness machine: the LLM does indeed return a web_fetch command with the correct URL and it's indeed correctly fetched by the harness' host. The target host also sees a connection coming from the correct source IP and there's also no scraping activity on the server afterwards - at least not yet. BUT: whenever I ask the LLM to look up the URL it just requested, I always get a chinese Alibaba cloud URL back: From the pcap I can tell that it's also not the harness somehow injecting the URL back into the LLM, since the first mention of aliyuncs.com in the pcap is the one after my "which URL did you fetch?" request. Does this happen to anyone else and can I get a sane explanation for this behaviour which is different from "those chinese models are spying on us"?!

items.title: RFC 0005 Phase 1: OpenCode pairing provenance capture prototype
items.body:
## What
The OpenCode + KITCH provenance capture prototype for RFC 0005 Phase 1. It records,
without ever fabricating a backend identity, the difference between the **configured**
model and the model/deployment that **actually answered**.

## Contents (prototype code)
- OpenCode plugin `.opencode/plugin/provpaws-capture.ts` — configured model per session.
- `tools/provcap-proxy.py` — loopback capture proxy: per-request response `model`,
  deployment header, serving endpoint, status; multi-file evidence log.
- `tools/prov.py` — `declare` evidence wiring: merges api+router evidence into an
  additive `session.capture` block (`log_digest`, `requests`, `window`, `endpoints`).
- `.provenance/schema/manifest-v2.schema.json` — additive schema 2.0 (`session.capture`,
  `observed[]`, `model_reported_by: router`); v1 stays valid.
- `tools/harness_cross_check.py` — harness `model:` pins vs provenance profiles.
- `.gitignore` — ignores `.provpaws/` + `provcap.jsonl`.
- `tools/test_prov.py` — capture-evidence, honesty-on-absent-endpoints, api/router
  trust, router-substitution-warn, v1/v2 guards (50+ tests).

## Review
The QA review lives on `develop`: `docs/research/rfc0005-opencode-pairing-review/`
(status report, honest implementation report, three-class trust grades, and §8 on
the tooling friction tracked in #165/#168).

## Known / honest gaps
- Backend identity is observed, never cryptographically verified — `verified` stays
  empty by design.
- A rebase orphans the manifest↔commit SHA name binding; `prov verify` does not catch
  it (see review Honest Report §7).

See the review pack on `develop` for the request-coverage table and the three-class
trust assessment.

items.title: WebFetch/WebSearch: intermittent HTTP 403 from routify-file-proxy-sg OSS layer and cross-request search result contamination
items.body:
# Summary

During a single agent session on 2026-10-06, the `WebFetch` and `WebSearch` tools exhibited two distinct failure modes, both pointing at the OSS-based fetch/cache proxy layer (`routify-file-proxy-sg.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com`):

1. **Intermittent `HTTP 403 Forbidden` on 5 of 11 `WebFetch` calls.** The requested targets were public GitHub REST API endpoints that were verifiably reachable; the requested URLs are transparently rewritten into signed OSS temporary-object URLs, which the proxy then rejects. An immediate retry of the identical requests in a new round succeeded.
2. **Cross-request result contamination in `WebSearch`.** A query about Go/MCP tooling returned 8 results belonging to a completely different, unrelated query (Chinese-language Bilibili content), with zero token overlap.

Both anomalies occurred within a ~20-minute window. Concurrent direct `curl` calls from the same machine to the same GitHub endpoints succeeded 5/5, ruling out GitHub-side rate limiting and local network issues.

# Environment

- Host: macOS (darwin/arm64), Node.js v24.16.0
- Agent: Yukino CLI, session date 2026-10-06
- Tools affected: `WebFetch` (5 of 11 calls failed), `WebSearch` (1 of 1 call returned contaminated results)
- All target URLs: `https://api.github.com/...` (public, unauthenticated REST endpoints)

# Anomaly 1 — WebFetch HTTP 403 Forbidden (5 failures in 2 batches)

## Batch A (3 parallel calls in one round — all failed)

Requested URLs:

- `https://api.github.com/repos/klauspost/compress`
- `https://api.github.com/repos/pelletier/go-toml`
- `https://api.github.com/repos/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk`

Final (rewritten) URLs reported in the errors — all `HTTP 403 Forbidden`:

```
https://routify-file-proxy-sg.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com/proxy_temp_file/production/2026-10-06/trace_21411c7a17909951401421554e0bd1/requestId_f2247c96a3d44441949246a8e33c8528/9e264d6ee413a1d15e02d58b64556849?Expires=1822099142&OSSAccessKeyId=LTAI5tKoG9A3DkwGD635QVZr&Signature=jUjwDc0G6tOq7lL58yQ9V9Z7p9c%3D
https://routify-file-proxy-sg.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com/proxy_temp_file/production/2026-10-06/trace_21411c7a17909951401421554e0bd1/requestId_f2247c96a3d44441949246a8e33c8528/1e33db4d92ba4dcd944a5b1a4a4b1a4de?Expires=1822099142&OSSAccessKeyId=LTAI5tKoG9A3DkwGD635QVZr&Signature=Q5j5Dz3V4Y2xq5Q5%2FvT9Y1jJZzA%3D
https://routify-file-proxy-sg.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com/proxy_temp_file/production/2026-10-06/trace_21411c7a17909951401421554e0bd1/requestId_f2247c96a3d44441949246a8e33c8528/44d1a4b06626a4b64c4d76e05b0b7f7f?Expires=1822099143&OSSAccessKeyId=LTAI5tKoG9A3DkwGD635QVZr&Signature=lD8m2nB4Q7cZ5V6R8tY1uI3oP0A%3D
```

## Batch B (2 parallel calls in a later round — all failed, new trace/request IDs)

Requested URLs:

- `https://api.github.com/repos/cloudwego/eino-ext/contents/components/tool`
- `https://api.github.com/repos/robfig/cron/releases?per_page=3`

Rewritten URLs reported in the errors:

```
https://routify-file-proxy-sg.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com/proxy_temp_file/production/2026-10-06/trace_21411c7a17909951669041738e0bd1/requestId_1c1a0a7648014f229694b3c3c5e06786/c53e3583d6f18442910a1c45008c1b55?Expires=1822099169&OSSAccessKeyId=LTAI5tKoG9A3DkwGD635QVZr&Signature=e1X0%2Fy%2Bg2k%2F6qQ8m%2F3vT9%2BcZzA%3D
https://routify-file-proxy-sg.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com/proxy_temp_file/production/2026-10-06/trace_21411c7a17909951669041738e0bd1/requestId_1c1a0a7648014f229694b3c3c5e06786/53b19b1824c9c89129c13e83f1c4d97b?Expires=1822099169&OSSAccessKeyId=LTAI5tKoG9A3DkwGD635QVZr&Signature=Ym4xR2%2B7pQ9vL3nK5tD8cJ6sA0E%3D
```

## Control group (same session, same proxy path — succeeded)

- Round 1 (3 parallel `WebFetch`): `api.github.com/repos/robfig/cron`, `.../twmb/murmur3`, `.../mark3labs/mcp-go` → all HTTP 200, correct JSON.
- Round 3 (**immediate retry of Batch A's identical 3 URLs**): all HTTP 200, correct JSON.
- Bash `curl` direct to `api.github.com` / `raw.githubusercontent.com` (5 calls, interleaved in time with the failures): all succeeded unauthenticated. A GitHub rate-limit 403 would come from `api.github.com` with a JSON body; these 403s were emitted by the OSS host itself, so GitHub-side throttling is ruled out.

# Anomaly 2 — WebSearch returned another query's results

- Query sent: `cloudwego eino-ext mcp tool mark3labs mcp-go official modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk migration` (num_results=8)
- Returned: 8 results, **all about Bilibili** — 52pojie.cn threads (a Bilibili 4K/8K video downloader, Bilibili Google Play APK re-uploads, a bilibili-helper Chrome extension, Bilibili TV edition version archives) and Zhihu questions (Bilibili danmaku blocklists, Bilibili documentaries, "how do you evaluate Bilibili today"). Item dates ranged 2019–2026, including relative timestamps ("2 days ago").
- Zero token overlap between the query and every returned title/URL/snippet.

This looks like the search path served a **different request's cached result set** (cache-key collision or request mix-up) in the same proxy/cache layer implicated by Anomaly 1. Note that silent contamination is arguably worse than a loud 403: wrong data can flow into agent reasoning unnoticed, whereas a 403 is at least detectable and retryable. The results were discarded in-session; the same research goal was accomplished via the GitHub `search/issues` REST API using `curl`.

# Analysis

1. **URL rewriting.** `WebFetch` transparently rewrites the requested URL into a signed OSS temporary object: `routify-file-proxy-sg.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com/proxy_temp_file/production/<date>/trace_<traceId>/requestId_<requestId>/<objectHash>?Expires=...&OSSAccessKeyId=...&Signature=...`.
2. **Not signature expiry.** `Expires=1822099142 / 1822099143 / 1822099169` decode to ≈ **2027-09-28** (far future). The 403s are therefore more likely a signature mismatch, a missing object (write/read race on the temp object), or a bucket policy rejection — not expired URLs.
3. **Failures are correlated per round.** In each failing round *all* parallel calls failed together; in successful rounds all succeeded together. This points at round-level proxy state (e.g., a bad cache node or signing-service instance serving that round) rather than per-request randomness.
4. **Retrying heals it.** Re-issuing the identical requests in a new round succeeded immediately, yet the tool surfaces the 403 to the model without any internal retry.
5. **Observability nit.** The error message helpfully exposes the final signed URL (that is how the proxy layer was identified), including the `OSSAccessKeyId`. An AccessKeyId is not a secret and pre-signed URLs are designed this way, so this is likely fine — flagged only so it can be confirmed that no session-scoped credentials ever leak through this error path.

# Expected behavior

- `WebFetch` of public, reachable endpoints should succeed reliably. On a transient proxy-layer 403/5xx, the tool should retry internally at least once (with a freshly signed URL) before surfacing an error to the model.
- `WebSearch` results must correspond to the submitted query. On cache miss/collision, the backend should fall back to a live query instead of returning another request's cached results. Consider a sanity check (e.g., cache entries keyed/validated by the exact query string) before serving cached search results.

# Steps to reproduce

Non-deterministic (intermittent proxy-layer fault). Observed sequence:

1. Start an agent session; issue a round of 3 parallel `WebFetch` calls to public `api.github.com` endpoints → succeeds.
2. Issue a second round of 3 parallel `WebFetch` calls to different `api.github.com/repos/*` endpoints → all 3 fail with 403 on the rewritten OSS URLs.
3. Immediately retry the identical 3 URLs in a new round → all succeed.
4. Later, issue 2 `WebFetch` calls (GitHub contents API + releases API) → both 403 again with a new trace/requestId; concurrent `curl` to the same endpoints succeeds.
5. Issue a `WebSearch` with a technical Go/MCP query → Bilibili-related results returned.

# Workaround

Fall back to `Bash` + `curl` for HTTP(S) fetches — worked 5/5 against `api.github.com`, `raw.githubusercontent.com`, and the GitHub search API during the same window.

Happy to provide the full raw tool transcript if helpful.

items.title: Return component data only for currently open component
items.body: https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/issues/19836 ## Summary by cubic Returns component data only for the currently open screen, shrinking the app package builders receive. - Screens other than the current one get their `_children` stripped and their `_rev` removed, so truncated screens can't be written, duplicated, or pasted into. Deletion keeps working because the server resolves the revision itself. - Previously loaded screens keep their full children when the package returns them truncated, and undoing deletion of a truncated screen restores its full children. - The builder refetches the package when the open screen changes, serialises initialisation, ignores stale responses, holds the preview while the package updates, and notifies when a screen fails to load. - Cut operations remove the component from its source screen during copy, so cutting and previewing no longer leave stale components behind. Cuts are atomic: failed saves restore the clipboard, and overlapping pastes never duplicate components. - Workspaces opened from project setup show a back button that returns to the query-provided return location. Written for commit 243fc49a0e7586ae7040f11397a06cd902942738. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: render_page/fetch_url fetch URLs the model invented: 11 renders of a made-up Alibaba OSS proxy URL in step 4, error pages taken as scene frames

labels.name: live-check
labels.description: Implemented; waiting for robin's live check (recipe in the ticket)

items.body:
## Symptom
In the 2026-09-24 diorama goal run, after the forced rollover at 20:37, the model called `render_page` **11 times** on URLs it made up. They point to a third-party Alibaba OSS file proxy (`http://routify-file-proxy-sg.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com/proxy_temp_file/production/2026-09-25/trace_…/requestId_…/<hash>.html?…`, some carrying `Expires=`/`OSSAccessKeyId`-style signing parameters). The deliverable is a local file (`work/chain.html`). Crow fetched every one of them from the internet, and the model read the returned "AccessDenied" XML error pages as frames of its own scene ("the only two frames that show anything else are the two XML error pages"). Step 4 was still open at 21:27, ~110 min in.

## Evidence
- `~/.local/state/crow/session/session.json` (segment after `rollover-20260924-203758`): `render_page` calls with a `routify-file-proxy` path at msgs 25, 37, 113, 131, 147, 157, 180, 196, 239, 243, 251. The captures from 21:18–21:20 (`render-20260924-211837/211919/212019.png`) come back `done`, 410–448 colours.
- Where the URLs came from: the string `routify` occurs **0** times in both earlier rollover segments, in `subtasks/`, and in any tool result before msg 25. msg 25 is the model's own tool call. The URL is **invented**, not copied.
- What left the machine with the requests: msg 25's query is the URL-encoded `<script>var INST = [w,12,48];</script>`, a fragment of the page's data block. The other queries are `w=`, `spp=`, `half=` and the fake signing parameters. No file content beyond that fragment, and no secret, was in any URL (all 11 checked).
- Mode was `yolo` (crow.log 18:01:42), so nothing asked. `tool_render_page` (`cli/crow_core.py:10807` at `5fbb86a`) accepts any `https?://` target that passes `_url_complaint` (`:13909`), which only rejects abbreviated hostnames (#203). `fetch_url` (`:13957`) uses the same guard.

## Attribution
The model hallucinated the URLs, and that is the root. Crow's gap is that it treats an invented remote URL like a real one. This is a **MEASURED FAILURE**: 11 outbound requests to a host nobody named, error pages taken as evidence, and time lost in step 4. Ruled out: a tool rewriting paths (the local-path results in the same segment are correct), and a delegate/subtask source (0 occurrences).

## Research
- Package and URL hallucination is a documented LLM failure. Spracklen et al. 2024, "We Have a Package for You!" (https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.10279), measure invented package names; the same mechanism produces invented but plausible URLs. The recommended mitigation is to check against a known source before acting. Read, not measured here.
- OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025, LLM06 Excessive Agency (https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/): limit what tools can reach to what the task needs.

## Proposed fix
Checked against `5fbb86a` (main).
- **A (chosen): provenance guard for remote URLs** in `render_page` and `fetch_url`. A remote host must already appear in this conversation: in the user's text, a tool result (search results, a fetched page's links, file contents read), or the goal/PLAN.md. Otherwise the call is refused with an actionable sentence: `refused: <host> appears nowhere in this conversation -- a URL you made up? This goal's page is local: pass its path (e.g. work/chain.html?shot=default).` A cheap host set is kept per chat, fed where tool results are recorded, and survives the rollover through the carried-across-the-cut block. Always on, including yolo: it is a sanity check, not an approval.
- **B:** ask before any remote URL in yolo. Rejected: yolo exists for AFK runs, and a question nobody answers stalls the run.
- **C:** block remote URLs entirely in goal mode. Rejected: research steps legitimately fetch docs.
- **Out of scope:** the model's tendency itself (sampling/prompt); #286 (judge rubric).

## Expected result
- Unit: `render_page("http://routify-file-proxy-sg.oss-…/x.html")` in a conversation that never mentioned the host → refused with the sentence above, and no browser starts. After a tool result containing `https://developer.mozilla.org/...`, `fetch_url` on that host passes. Red without the fix.
- Live: in the next diorama run, crow.log/session show 0 remote `render_page` calls to hosts not present in the conversation.

items.title: feat(core): send session ID to Routify endpoints
items.body:
## What this PR does

Adds the active Qwen Code session ID as the `session_id` request header for HTTPS LLM calls to the three ModelRouter endpoints documented by Routify: `routify.alibaba-inc.com`, `routify-online.alibaba-inc.com`, and `routify-pub.alibaba-inc.com`.

The session value is resolved for every request, so `/clear` and other session changes are reflected without rebuilding the model client. OpenAI-compatible, DashScope, Anthropic, Gemini, and Vertex request paths are covered. Existing request headers and proxy-aware fetch behavior are preserved.

The destination check is intentionally fixed and exact. Subdomains, lookalike hosts, plain HTTP URLs, and all other providers do not receive the header.

## Why it's needed

Routify's ModelRouter accepts `session_id` for session affinity, traffic marking, and troubleshooting. The supplied AP recreation log contains 37 Anthropic requests to `routify-pub.alibaba-inc.com`, but none includes any affinity header documented by ModelRouter. Reusing Qwen Code's existing session ID lets ModelRouter keep requests from one CLI session correlated without introducing another identifier.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Point each supported provider protocol at one of the three HTTPS Routify endpoints and capture the outbound request. Confirm that it contains one non-empty `session_id` header while authorization and content headers remain unchanged.
2. Start a new session with `/clear` and send another request. Confirm that `session_id` changes to the new active session value.
3. Point the same provider at a subdomain, a lookalike `alibaba-inc.com` hostname, a plain HTTP Routify URL, or an unrelated provider. Confirm that `session_id` is absent.
4. Run the focused core tests. The local run passed 392 tests across exact-host matching and all SDK integration paths.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A (no UI change). Before: all 37 requests in the supplied Routify AP recreation log lacked a documented affinity header. After: focused tests confirm the header is added only to the three exact HTTPS Routify destinations and follows session rotation. A live request was not replayed because the supplied archive contains a plaintext bearer token.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Local Node.js 24.18.0, no sandbox. `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, targeted ESLint, and 392 focused unit tests passed.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Routify receives a stable identifier across requests in one Qwen Code session. Exposure is limited to the three exact documented HTTPS hostnames; there is no suffix match, wildcard, or user-configurable broadcast.
- Not validated / out of scope: live post-change Routify traffic, Windows/Linux runtime verification, non-LLM traffic, MCP/tool requests, request IDs, trace propagation, and body metadata.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Related to #4384.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

为发往 Routify 文档列出的三个 ModelRouter 端点的 HTTPS 大模型请求增加当前 Qwen Code 会话 ID，使用的请求头是 `session_id`。三个端点分别是 `routify.alibaba-inc.com`、`routify-online.alibaba-inc.com` 和 `routify-pub.alibaba-inc.com`。

每次请求都会读取当前会话值，因此执行 `/clear` 或发生其它会话切换后，无需重建模型客户端即可使用新的值。OpenAI 兼容、DashScope、Anthropic、Gemini 和 Vertex 请求链路均已覆盖，同时保留已有请求头和支持代理的 fetch 行为。

目标地址检查采用固定的精确匹配。子域名、相似域名、普通 HTTP 地址以及其它所有模型服务都不会收到该请求头。

## 为什么需要这个改动

Routify 的 ModelRouter 支持使用 `session_id` 做会话亲和、流量染色和问题排查。用户提供的 AP 复现日志中有 37 个发往 `routify-pub.alibaba-inc.com` 的 Anthropic 请求，但均未携带 ModelRouter 文档列出的任何亲和请求头。复用 Qwen Code 已有的会话 ID，可以在不新增标识符的情况下，让 ModelRouter 关联同一个 CLI 会话中的请求。

## Reviewer 测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 将各支持的模型协议分别指向三个 Routify HTTPS 端点之一并抓取出站请求，确认请求中有且仅有一个非空 `session_id`，同时认证头和内容相关请求头保持不变。
2. 通过 `/clear` 创建新会话后再次发送请求，确认 `session_id` 已更新为新的当前会话值。
3. 将同一个模型服务指向子域名、相似的 `alibaba-inc.com` 域名、普通 HTTP Routify 地址或无关模型服务，确认请求中没有 `session_id`。
4. 运行核心包定向测试。本地共通过 392 项测试，覆盖精确域名匹配和所有 SDK 集成链路。

### 证据（改动前后）

不适用（无 UI 改动）。改动前：用户提供的 Routify AP 复现日志中 37 个请求均未携带文档所列亲和请求头。改动后：定向测试确认仅三个精确的 HTTPS Routify 目标会添加该请求头，并且会话切换后值会更新。由于用户提供的压缩包中含有明文 bearer token，没有重放真实线上请求。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

### 环境（可选）

本地 Node.js 24.18.0，无沙箱。`npm run build`、`npm run typecheck`、定向 ESLint 以及 392 项定向单元测试均通过。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：Routify 会收到同一个 Qwen Code 会话内跨请求稳定的标识符。暴露范围仅限文档列出的三个精确 HTTPS 主机名，不存在后缀匹配、通配或用户可配置的全量广播。

items.title: Fix images/videos silently keeping a temporary third-party URL on R2-persist failure
items.body:
## Summary
Real production bug from the logs you shared: `nano_banana_2` image generation failed with `403 Client Error: Forbidden` fetching a third-party temp URL (`routify-file-proxy`, Aliyun OSS) passed as a reference image.

**Root cause**: `persistImagesToR2`/`persistVideoToR2` download a model's raw output and re-upload it to our own R2 for permanence — but if that single download attempt failed for any reason, the code silently returned the **original temporary third-party URL** as if it were a normal permanent one. That URL then got stored in conversation history and reused later (e.g. as a character reference for a new scene) — by which point the temporary URL's access had become invalid, causing exactly this 403 on a request that had nothing wrong with it itself.

## Fix
Retry the download up to 3 times with backoff (handles transient network blips), and if it still fails, throw a real error instead of silently returning the broken temp URL — this surfaces as a normal generation failure with credits refunded (existing error handling already does this), which is far better than a "successful" image that silently breaks whenever it's reused later.

Note: this only prevents new instances of the bug — any already-broken reference URLs stored in existing project histories (like the "ghd" project's character reference) will need to be regenerated fresh.

## Test plan

items.title: feat(security): block named Alibaba bucket, add novel-egress signal (FRE-1330)
items.body:
## Summary

- Closes FRE-1330: block the specific Alibaba OSS bucket a model emitted an unexplained
  `fetch_url` call to during a live turn, and add an observe-only signal for the next time this
  happens with a destination we've never seen before.
- No separate ADR — design intent is the ticket's own "Proposed shape" section.

- **Targeted block**: add the exact bucket hostname
  (`routify-file-proxy-sg.oss-ap-southeast-1.aliyuncs.com`) to `DomainGuard`'s bundled
  blocklist (`src/personal_agent/security.py`). Refused pre-connection, logged as
  `fetch_url_blocked` — the existing code path, unchanged.
- **Novel-destination signal**: new `NovelDestinationTracker` in `security.py`. On every
  `fetch_url` call, checks whether the target's registrable domain (eTLD+1) has been seen in
  the prior 14 days (`AGENT_URL_GUARD_NOVELTY_WINDOW_DAYS`); if not, logs a distinct
  `fetch_url_novel_destination` event and records the sighting. Disk-persisted
  (`telemetry/security/egress_novelty_seen.json`), survives restarts. Observe-only — never
  blocks — and fail-open: a tracker I/O failure is caught and logged, never propagates into
  the fetch itself.
- **Fold-in fix**: `DomainGuard._refresh()`'s disk-cache branch was replacing `_blocklist`
  with the cached URLhaus set alone, without unioning `_BUNDLED_BLOCKLIST` (the network-fetch
  branch already did this union; the disk-cache branch didn't match it). A stale-but-valid
  disk cache predating this deploy would have silently dropped the new block on the next warm
  reload, for up to an hour. Found during codex plan-review, not by hypothesis — fixed because
  it directly undermines AC-3's "the named bucket is blocked" as a durable guarantee, with its
  own regression test.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC-1 — first-ever destination produces a distinct, queryable signal.**
  Mechanism proven by unit test (`tests/test_security/test_novelty_tracker.py`): first
  `check_and_record()` call for a domain returns `novel=True` and persists it to disk; wired
  into `fetch_url_executor` so a fresh domain logs `fetch_url_novel_destination`
  (`tests/personal_agent/tools/test_fetch.py::test_fre1330_fresh_domain_logs_novel_destination_event`).
  The ticket explicitly requires live ES visibility too ("fails if demonstrated only by unit
  test") — that half is a post-deploy verification step (see the Linear handoff comment); a
  build-worktree session has no live ES to query against.
- **AC-2 — seeded negative.** A domain already seen inside the window does not re-alert:
  `test_repeat_sighting_inside_window_is_not_novel`,
  `test_fre1330_repeat_domain_does_not_log_novel_destination_event`. Same live-ES caveat as
  AC-1 for the "no alert fires" half.
- **AC-3 — the named bucket is blocked, with the block observed.**
  `test_fre1330_named_bucket_refused_before_connection` attempts the actual fetch through
  `fetch_url_executor` against the ticket's literal URL, with the HTTP transport patched to
  fail the test if reached — proves refusal, not a 403 from the origin. Paired with
  `test_bundled_entry_survives_a_stale_predating_disk_cache` for the fold-in fix.
- **AC-4 — the long tail still works.** All 22 destinations from the ticket's call history are
  parametrized against `DomainGuard.check_url()`
  (`test_fre1330_long_tail_host_still_allowed_by_guard`), plus one full end-to-end
  `fetch_url_executor` pass for a representative host
  (`test_fre1330_long_tail_host_end_to_end_not_blocked`).

## Pre-merge checklist

- [x] Tests passing (`make test`) — 8451 passed; the 8 pre-existing failures on this run are
      confirmed present on a clean `origin/main` checkout too (verified via `git stash`), no
      new failures introduced by this diff
- [x] `make mypy` clean
- [x] `make ruff-check` + `make ruff-format` clean
- [x] `pre-commit run --all-files` clean
- [x] ADR / spec linked above (if architectural) — N/A, ticket itself is the design doc
- [x] Screenshots attached (if UI change) — N/A
- [x] Joinability probe green in CI (if change touches event emit, cost recording, memory
      writes, or schema — ADR-0074) — N/A, no schema/memory-write change
- [x] Identity tuple threaded on new emit sites (`session_id`, `trace_id` — ADR-0074) —
      `fetch.py`'s new `fetch_url_novel_destination` log carries `trace_id` like every other
      event in that file; `NovelDestinationTracker`'s own internal warnings are
      module-global/background-scoped (no request context), matching `DomainGuard`'s existing
      trace_id-less warnings in the same file

## Test plan

```
uv run pytest tests/test_security/test_novelty_tracker.py tests/test_security/test_domain_guard.py tests/personal_agent/tools/test_fetch.py tests/personal_agent/telemetry/test_mount_coverage.py tests/scripts/test_config_inventory.py -v
make test
make mypy
make ruff-check
pre-commit run --all-files
```

**Diff class: escalated** — production security/governance code in `fetch_url`'s egress guard
(turn path for every `fetch_url` call). Flagged for owner `/code-review ultra` before merge.

items.title: feat(core): add forceGlobalCacheScope for Anthropic proxy providers
items.body:
## Summary

Closes #6642

Allow users to opt-in to `scope: 'global'` on Anthropic `cache_control` entries even when the base URL is not an Anthropic-native origin (e.g. proxy providers like Routify, OpenRouter). This enables cross-session prompt caching through proxies that forward the `prompt-caching-scope-2026-01-05` beta.

## Problem

Currently `useGlobalCacheScope()` only returns `true` for `*.anthropic.com` base URLs. Proxy users are stuck with per-session cache scope, resulting in ~20% cache hit rates and 3-4x higher input token costs.

## Solution

Add a new `forceGlobalCacheScope` field to `ContentGeneratorConfig` that bypasses the native-baseURL check. Users opt in via their model's `generationConfig`:

```json
{
  "modelProviders": {
    "anthropic": {
      "models": [
        {
          "id": "claude-sonnet-4-20250514",
          "baseUrl": "https://proxy.routify.ai/v1",
          "generationConfig": {
            "enableCacheControl": true,
            "forceGlobalCacheScope": true
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `core/contentGenerator.ts` | Add `forceGlobalCacheScope` to `ContentGeneratorConfig` |
| `anthropicContentGenerator.ts` | Update `useGlobalCacheScope()` to check the new field |
| `models/constants.ts` | Add to `MODEL_GENERATION_CONFIG_FIELDS` |
| `models/types.ts` | Add to `ModelGenerationConfig` Pick type |
| `config/config.ts` | Wire through `handleModelChange` hot-update path |
| `anthropicContentGenerator.test.ts` | 2 tests: opt-in on proxy URL + suppression when caching disabled |

## Tests

- 145/145 Anthropic converter tests pass
- TypeScript compilation: 0 errors
- New tests verify:
  1. `forceGlobalCacheScope: true` on non-Anthropic URL → emits `scope: 'global'` + beta header
  2. `enableCacheControl: false` + `forceGlobalCacheScope: true` → no cache_control emitted (safety)

items.title: fix(core): stop implying global cache scope on Anthropic-native baseURLs (#15039)
items.body:
## What this PR does

Stops an Anthropic-native baseURL from implying `cache_control: { scope: 'global' }`. The native default is now session scope (no `scope` field), which the API accepts and which still caches; `scope: 'global'` stays an explicit opt-in via `forceGlobalCacheScope` for proxy providers that forward the `prompt-caching-scope-2026-01-05` beta.

Concretely, `useGlobalCacheScope()` no longer returns true for a native baseURL — only for `forceGlobalCacheScope === true`. The beta header is unaffected: it is gated on the assembled body (`hasGlobalCacheScopeOnWire`), so the beta and the body field stay in agreement either way.

## Why it's needed

The Anthropic API rejects a `scope: 'global'` breakpoint whose preceding blocks are unmarked (`cache_control.scope: "global" is only valid when every preceding block is also globally scoped`). Our request shape marks only the **last tool** plus `system[0]`, so with more than one tool an unmarked tool precedes the global-scoped one — and the first prompt of every session failed with HTTP 400 against `api.anthropic.com` (issue #15039, with a captured request body and a minimal reproducer).

The 4-breakpoint cap is what rules out the alternative of marking every tool, so session scope is the native default.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/core/anthropicContentGenerator` — 198/198.
2. `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/core/anthropicContentGenerator src/config/settings.test.ts` — 332/332.
3. Reviewer probe against a live endpoint: with `authType: anthropic` and `baseUrl: https://api.anthropic.com`, a first prompt that previously returned `400 … "cache_control.scope: \"global\"` is only valid when every preceding block is also globally scoped` should now succeed, with no `scope` field on any block.
4. The regression direction is pinned by the new cases: re-adding `isAnthropicNativeBaseUrl(...) ||` to `useGlobalCacheScope()` turns `keeps session scope on an Anthropic-native baseURL by default (#15039)` red.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no user-visible surface; the behavior change is on the request wire (`scope` field + beta header).

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |   N/A  |

### Environment (optional)

N/A — unit tests only; the endpoint check needs an Anthropic key.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a native endpoint loses the cross-session **tool-prefix** cache that `scope: 'global'` was meant to provide. The tool prefix is the largest, slowest-changing block, so this is the hit-rate we give up on native endpoints — the alternative (marking every tool) exceeds the 4-breakpoint cap. The reporter explicitly left the suffix/user-turn scope question open, so the shape of the opt-in path is a product call, not one this PR makes.
- Not validated / out of scope: the **opt-in** path is unchanged — with `forceGlobalCacheScope: true` the last tool still carries `scope: 'global'`, which an Anthropic-enforcing endpoint rejects once more than one tool is present. Proxy providers that forward the beta are the intended audience for the opt-in and are unaffected by that rule. If a native user opts in, they need the marker placement revisited (the API accepts global scope on `system[0]` + the user turn without any tool marks, per the issue's replays) — that is the follow-up question, not a silent change here.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: requests to Anthropic-native endpoints no longer carry `scope: 'global'` and no longer send the `prompt-caching-scope-2026-01-05` beta. Prompt caching itself is unchanged (per-session `cache_control` still ships). Users who relied on the native default to get the scope beta must set `forceGlobalCacheScope: true` — and then the tool-prefix caveat above applies.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15039.

items.title: serve's end-of-generation accounting is wrong three ways: toolcall give_up flushes malformed markup with no WARN (4 of 8 malformed calls on 2026-09-22 were silent), a cut named call is delivered twice (salvaged call + its raw markup as content, 6,986 tokens at 10:23), and a client disconnect is logged as finish=length plus a false 'ERROR BUG'
items.body:
## Symptom

On 2026-09-22 the engine's own record of how a generation ended was wrong in three ways. Each one misleads the #91 instruments, anyone reading engine.log, and the client.

1. **Malformed tool calls go out silently.** Only 4 of the day's malformed calls got the `MALFORMED tool call` WARN. At least 4 more reached Crow as raw markup content with no line at all. So the log undercounts what robin saw in the GUI by half. (#91's in-vivo comment counts "4× MALFORMED" from this same log.)
2. **A malformed call is sent twice.** When a named call is cut off (EOS inside a parameter), the client gets the salvaged call (`Call` plus `_truncated` args) **and** the call's entire raw markup as `content`. At 10:23:37 that was 6,986 tokens of a runaway URL, delivered twice.
3. **A client disconnect is logged as `finish: length`, plus a false `ERROR … BUG`.** An aborted generation keeps the default finish `"length"` in the `[chat]` line and in the routing JSON. The TASK K invariant check then reports the unterminated argument fragments as an engine bug.

## Evidence

engine.log (`~/.local/state/crow/logs/engine.log`, UTC), crow-nest b6d57f8:

**(1) The silent give_up path.** Stop rounds with `content chunks 1 … tool chunks 0 … tool calls 0` at 15:17:12, 15:20:04, 15:39:50 and 15:45:28 (8, 8, 8 and 11 tokens) have no WARN. The client stored exactly `<tool_call>\n\n</function>\n</tool_call>` for them (Crow `session.json` msgs 71, 139, 469, 561). Only the 15:16:42 round (msg 65) got `WARN chat: [chat] MALFORMED tool call`.

Cause: `ToolStream::finish` (`engine/src/toolcall.rs:470`) returns `true`, and so triggers the WARN at `bin/serve.rs:3869`, only when the stream **ends** inside a call. When `</tool_call>` arrives in state `Func` before any `<function=` (`toolcall.rs:765-770`), or a name or parameter name is invalid (`:790`, `:830`), `give_up` (`:712`) flushes the raw markup as content and returns without a trace. The generation then ends in `Text`, and `finish` returns `false`.

**(2) Raw markup after a salvaged call.** 10:23:37: `WARN … MALFORMED tool call`, then `prompt 132431 tok … generated 6986 tok … finish stop, content chunks 58 … tool chunks 6920 … tool calls 0`. Crow's transcript (`rollover-20260922-123048.md:3794-3800`) holds the assistant content `<tool_call>\n<function=read_image>\n<parameter=path>\nhttp://routify-file-proxy…` **and** the structured `read_image` call with the same value.

Cause: `finish` calls `close_args_truncated` and then `flush_raw` (`toolcall.rs:497-509`). `flush_raw` emits the raw markup as content whenever `self.index == 0`. It ignores `self.named`, while `content()` (`:511`) drops text exactly when `self.named`. The doc table at `toolcall.rs:35-41` says the raw markup goes out "before the first call". Here the first call had already been emitted as `Emit::Call`.

**(3) Client gone.**
- 13:58:31: `ERROR chat: [chat] BUG: the arguments of tool call 0 are not a JSON object - serde_json: EOF while parsing a string at line 1 column 900`, then `finish length, … client gone`, then routing `"finish":"length","predicted_n":304`.
- 15:54:30: `WARN write failed, aborting the generation: Connection reset by peer`, then `generated 2 tok … finish length … client gone` (robin closed the window).

Neither request was near its `max_tokens`. Cause: `let mut finish = "length";` (`bin/serve.rs:3600`) is never overwritten on the abort paths (`aborted = true` at `:3698`, `:3744`, `:3796`, `:3804`, `:3816`). `ts.finish()` is skipped when `aborted` (`:3786`), so `args_acc` is left unterminated, and the invariant loop (`:3855-3861`) logs it as an engine BUG.

The older logs show the same pattern: `backup-cleantest-20260922-085226/logs` has 4× `ERROR … BUG: the arguments … EOF while parsing a string` and 18 `write failed` / `Broken pipe` aborts.

## Attribution

crow-nest (serve's end-of-generation accounting and `toolcall.rs`'s flush rule). The malformed markup itself is the model's, and #91 covers that class. Crow's handling of degenerate rounds is Crow #217. This ticket covers only what the engine **reports**.

## Research

- vLLM reports client disconnects as their own finish class: the abort path ends a stream with `finish_reason="abort"`, and fixes keep that reason from being overwritten (vllm PR #47933, https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47933; xorbitsai/inference#5548/#5549 on aborting on disconnect). A disconnect is not `length`, and statistics that mix the two are wrong.
- vLLM's Qwen tool parsers have had the same class of defects: a call left in `content` while `tool_calls` stays empty, or tool calls lost from the stream (vllm#22975 https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/22975, vllm#58105 https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58105). The fixes converge on one rule: a byte of the call ends up either in `tool_calls` or in `content`, never in both, and every parse failure is counted.
- OpenAI's `finish_reason` contract: `stop`, `length`, `tool_calls`, `content_filter`. A stream the client abandoned never gets a finish chunk at all, so the value is purely a server-side record and should say what happened.

## Proposed fix

1. **One counter for every malformed path.** `give_up` sets `self.malformed += 1` (a new field), and `finish` returns `malformed > 0 || <today's condition>`. Or add `fn malformed(&self) -> usize` and have serve read it. The WARN at `bin/serve.rs:3869` names the path (`eos-in-call`, `close-before-function`, `bad-name`, `bad-param-name`), and the `[chat]` summary line gets `malformed N`. Test: `<tool_call>\n\n</function>\n</tool_call>` (the live shape) counts 1.
2. **No double delivery.** In `flush_raw` (`toolcall.rs:497`), treat `self.named` like `self.index > 0`: the call already went out as `Emit::Call`, so its raw markup is dropped and counted in `dropped`, not emitted as content. Update the doc table at `:35-41` ("before the first call **was named**"). Test: EOS inside `<parameter=path>` after a name emits `Call` plus `_truncated` args and **no** `Content`.
3. **Say "aborted".** On every `aborted = true` path, set `finish = "abort"` for the log line and the routing JSON (`bin/serve.rs:3600` onward; the wire never carries it, because the client is gone). Skip the TASK K invariant loop (`:3855`) when `aborted`, since an unterminated fragment there is a disconnect, not an engine bug. Or run `ts.finish()` into a throw-away vec so the accumulator closes.
4. Optional: add `"_truncated_by": "stop" | "length"` beside `_truncated` in `close_args_truncated` (`toolcall.rs:659`). A client then gets the reason from the arguments alone, which helps the llama.cpp-parity path that has no `finish_reason` per call.

## Expected result

engine.log counts every malformed call. It would have said 8, not 4, on 2026-09-22. A cut-off named call reaches the client once, not twice. Disconnects appear as `finish: abort` with no `ERROR … BUG`, so the routing statistics and the #91 instruments stop counting robin's window closes as length cuts.

items.title: fix(core): surface the provider request id on bodyless API errors

items.body:
# Pull Request

## What this PR does

Surfaces the provider request id on the user-facing API error line, so a bodyless provider rejection is traceable.

Before: `[API Error: 400 status code (no body)]`
After: `[API Error: 400 status code (no body) (request_id: a30a1854-1925-4da8-8803-73fee2865116)]`

The id is not new information — openai-node already stamps `x-request-id` onto every `APIError`'s `headers`. It was being discarded in `Turn.run`'s catch block, which builds a `StructuredError` from `getErrorMessage()` / `getErrorStatus()` and throws the original `Error` away. Six of the seven `parseAndFormatApiError` call sites pass a `StructuredError` or an already-flattened string, so no formatter-only change could ever reach the id. This PR resolves it upstream while the `Error` is still whole:

- `StructuredError` gains an optional `requestId`, populated in `Turn.run`'s catch from the **raw** caught error, before `toFriendlyError()` can substitute an `Error` that no longer carries `.headers`.
- New `resolveApiErrorRequestId()` reads either that resolved field or a live error's headers, reusing `retryPolicy.getHeaderValue` (now exported) so both a real `Headers` instance and a plain record work.
- `parseAndFormatApiError` appends ` (request_id: ...)` **inside** the closing bracket, and skips the suffix when the message already embeds the id (the Responses API error paths print it themselves, so the suffix would repeat it).

Note the suffix is not limited to the bodyless case in the title: it lands on any structured or live error with a resolvable id (e.g. `[API Error: API key not valid… (Status: INVALID_ARGUMENT) (request_id: …)]`), which also changes the error text inside `--output-format json` for errors carrying an id. That broader behavior is deliberate — the bodyless case is just where the id was completely invisible.

## Why it's needed

Reported in #14115. A strict OpenAI-compatible backend (vLLM/SGLang-backed, e.g. TheHive AI) rejects a request with a 400 whose body openai-node 5.11.0 fails to capture, so the CLI shows only `400 status code (no body)`. The user has nothing to quote to their provider, which makes every such rejection undiagnosable — and the related request-shape issues (#14112, #12878, #13807, #13853) all get harder to triage as a result.

Two details that are easy to get wrong, both covered here:

- **Bracket access silently fails.** `APIError.headers` is a genuine `Headers` instance, which has no own enumerable properties, so `error.headers['x-request-id']` reads `undefined`. That trap is what produced the misleading `headers: {}` inspect artifact in the issue thread. Reusing `getHeaderValue` handles `.get()` and plain records (case-insensitively).
- **Placement matters for idempotency.** `isAlreadyFormatted()` keys off `endsWith(']')`. A suffix *after* the closing bracket would defeat that guard and risk `[API Error: [API Error: ...]]` on the second pass through `cli/src/utils/errors.ts`. Putting it inside the bracket keeps the guard working with no change to it.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

The tests were written first and confirmed red on unmodified `91385884eb` (fresh `origin/main`):

```
× parseAndFormatApiError > request id surfacing > appends an already-resolved StructuredError.requestId
  → expected '[API Error: 400 status code (no body)]' to be '[API Error: 400 status code (no body) (request_id: …)]'
× parseAndFormatApiError > request id surfacing > reads x-request-id off a live error carrying a real Headers instance
× parseAndFormatApiError > request id surfacing > reads x-request-id off a live error carrying a plain header record
× parseAndFormatApiError > request id surfacing > reads X-Request-Id off a live error carrying a plain header record
× parseAndFormatApiError > request id surfacing > keeps the 429 quota guidance after the request id
× parseAndFormatApiError > request id surfacing > bounds an over-long provider-supplied request id
× Turn > run > request id on the Error event > carries x-request-id from a real Headers instance
× Turn > run > request id on the Error event > carries x-request-id from a plain header record
```

The `turn.test.ts` cases are the load-bearing ones: they drive `sendMessageStream`'s rejection path and assert the yielded `LlmEventType.Error` value carries the id. A formatter-only fix passes the `errorParsing` cases and still shows nothing in the TUI, which is why the end-to-end assertion exists.

After the fix:

```
 ✓ src/utils/retryPolicy.test.ts (20 tests) 16ms
 ✓ src/utils/errorParsing.test.ts (35 tests) 13ms
 ✓ src/core/turn.test.ts (50 tests) 40ms

 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  105 passed (105)
```

Both header shapes are covered end to end (real `Headers` and plain record, plus `x-request-id` / `X-Request-Id` casing on the record path, since `Headers.get()` is case-insensitive but a record is not). Regression vectors explicitly covered: the `endsWith(']')` idempotency guard (no double-wrap), the existing 429 quota suffix still appending after the id, and no doubled id on the Responses API paths that already embed it. Nothing asserts on `util.inspect` output of a `Headers` object.

Reproduce locally:

```
cd packages/core
node ../../node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run \
  src/utils/errorParsing.test.ts src/core/turn.test.ts src/utils/retryPolicy.test.ts \
  --coverage.enabled=false
```

### Evidence (Before & After)

```
Before: [API Error: 400 status code (no body)]
After:  [API Error: 400 status code (no body) (request_id: a30a1854-1925-4da8-8803-73fee2865116)]
```

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment

Unit tests only (Linux, Node v24.19.0). No live-provider run — the reporter offered to test a patch against their endpoint.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: `requestId` is appended to a user-visible string. It is bounded to 128 chars (following the bounded-excerpt precedent in `responses-http-error.ts`) so a misconfigured or hostile `x-request-id` cannot spill an arbitrary-length string into the error line. ASCII only — no em dash — because the reporter is on Windows 11 where console encoding is a real hazard.
- Not validated / out of scope: **the raw `errorResponse` body (layer 2 of the issue) is deliberately not added.** The reporter proved with a fetch-wrapper probe that the 435-byte JSON body reaches fetch but is lost *inside* openai-node 5.11.0 — `errorResponse` is `undefined` and the SDK message is literally `"400 status code (no body)"`. An `errorResponse` field would therefore render empty for exactly the backends in scope, so it needs an upstream openai-node fix first. Also untouched: `getRequestId` in `openaiContentGenerator/errorHandler.ts`, which already works — the reporter's own captured `OPENAI_ERROR` record contained `requestId: 'f423f517-…'`. No fallback is added for `APIConnectionError`, which genuinely arrives without headers.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. `StructuredError.requestId` is optional and conditionally spread, so the field is absent (not `undefined`-valued) when no id exists and existing `toEqual` assertions on that shape are unaffected. `retryPolicy.getHeaderValue` changed from module-private to exported with no behavior change; it is not re-exported from the package barrel.

## Linked Issues

Refs #14115

## 中文说明

本 PR 在用户可见的 API 错误行上显示 provider 的 request id，使无 body 的 provider 拒绝可追溯。修复前 CLI 只显示 `400 status code (no body)`，用户没有任何可以提供给 provider 排查的信息；修复后显示 `[API Error: 400 status code (no body) (request_id: …)]`。

实现方式：`Turn.run` 的 catch 块在原始 `Error`（还带有 `.headers`）被丢弃之前解析 `x-request-id`，存入 `StructuredError.requestId`；formatter 在闭合中括号内追加该 id（保持幂等保护有效），若消息本身已内嵌该 id 则跳过后缀避免重复打印。同时补齐模板要求的中文说明区块，并在描述中明确：后缀不限于 bodyless 场景，对所有能解析出 id 的错误生效，`--output-format json` 中带 id 错误的文本也随之变化。

items.title: 分类器报错

labels.name: status/needs-triage
labels.description: Issue needs to be triaged and labeled

items.body:
### What happened?

Under `tools.approvalMode = "auto"`, the safety classifier persistently fail-closes and **blocks every approval-requiring tool** (run_shell_command / write_file / agent / web_fetch), creating a **deadlock** — even the write_file/edit needed to change settings and recover is blocked.

Setup: fastModel = `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6-20260217` (a Claude 4.6 adaptive-thinking model), main model = claude-opus-4-8, both via an Anthropic-native base URL (`.../protocol/anthropic`, i.e. `/v1/messages`).

Enabling `QWEN_DEBUG_LOG_FILE`, `~/.qwen/debug/<sessionId>.txt` repeatedly shows:

```
[WARN] [CLASSIFIER] failClosed stage=fast reason="Classifier stage 1 unavailable - blocked for safety" cause="Error: Invalid side query response: params must have required property 'shouldBlock'"
[WARN] [TOOL_SCHEDULER] Auto mode blocked (classifier_unavailable): tool=run_shell_command/write_file/agent/web_fetch
```

Every failure is preceded by a long run of `[GEMINI_STREAM] [THOUGHT_MERGE] Accumulating thought ...` ending in `type=gemini_thought` — the classifier side query received only thinking content, no structured tool_use result. It is **intermittent** (same session has both successes and failures). Reproduced repeatedly on 0.19.10 **after a restart**, so "restart fixes it" is false.

**Root cause (client-side, three factors compounding), verified against 0.19.10 bundled source:**

The classifier uses fastModel to send a structured side query that must return `{shouldBlock}` (`classifyAction` → `runSideQuery` → `generateJson`, schema requires `shouldBlock`). Sonnet 4.6 produces no structured result → schema validation fails → `failClosed`.

1. **generateJson never sets `tool_choice`.** `generateJson` (chunk-K7CRWKOE.js:31601) wraps the schema as a `respond_in_schema` tool, but the Anthropic-native generator's `buildRequest` (anthropicContentGenerator-*.js:5220) returns `{ model, system, messages, tools, ...sampling, ...thinking, ...outputConfig }` — **no `tool_choice` anywhere in that file**. Anthropic defaults to `tool_choice: auto`, so the model may legitimately emit only thinking/text and never call the tool. When no functionCall is found and text isn't valid JSON, generateJson returns `{}` → missing `shouldBlock`. (The OpenAI-compat layer, chunk-V7EQTZYR.js:2362, DOES support tool_choice; the native Anthropic branch has no equivalent forced-tool path.)
2. **max_tokens is squeezed to 32.** The classifier passes `maxOutputTokens: 32`; `reconcileMaxTokens(28000, 32)` (chunk-B7NUUEXC.js:222, `Math.min`) = 32. A tiny output budget for a model that emits thinking first.
3. **Sonnet 4.6 is an adaptive-thinking model.** `buildThinkingConfig` (:5403) correctly returns undefined when `includeThoughts===false` (so qwen is NOT sending a thinking param), but `modelSupportsAdaptiveThinking()` (:5359, major 4.6+) is true — thinking is server-driven, so the model still emits thinking blocks that consume the 32-token budget before any tool_use.

Compounded: no forced tool_choice + server-side adaptive thinking consuming output + 32-token budget → no `respond_in_schema` tool_use → generateJson returns `{}` → missing `shouldBlock` → `failClosed`.

**Ruled out:**
- Not a gateway/routify issue — standard `/v1/messages`, gateway only forwards; control tests returned HTTP 200.
- Not a fastModel `anthropic:` prefix syntax issue — `parseModelIdSelector` (chunk-K7CRWKOE.js:30709) uses `AUTH_TYPES.has()`; the `provider:id` prefix is officially supported and resolves correctly.
- Not fixed by restart/upgrade — still reproduces on 0.19.10 after restart.

**Not 100% pinned:** debug logs don't record the wire request/response body, so "32-token budget exhausted by thinking" vs "model chose not to call the tool" isn't directly verified. But the attribution (client-side request construction × adaptive-thinking) is certain.


### What did you expect to happen?


The auto-mode classifier should reliably obtain a `{shouldBlock}` decision when fastModel is an Anthropic adaptive-thinking model, instead of fail-closing and deadlocking all approval-requiring tools.

Concretely:
1. For the classifier's structured side query, **force `tool_choice`** on the Anthropic-native branch (e.g. `{type:"tool", name:"respond_in_schema"}` or `{type:"any"}`) so the model must emit a structured tool call.
2. **Don't clamp the classifier's max_tokens to 32** — leave enough budget for possible thinking + tool_use.
3. **Surface the underlying cause** in the user-visible failure (today the real cause only goes to `QWEN_DEBUG_LOG_FILE`; the terminal shows only "Classifier stage 1 unavailable - blocked for safety").
4. **Avoid the deadlock:** when the classifier is unavailable, allow self-recovery actions (edit settings / switch approval mode / switch fastModel) through an exempt path.


### Client information


Qwen Code: 0.19.10 (095bd1609)
运行环境: Node.js v22.23.1 / npm 11.6.2
LSP: disabled
操作系统: darwin arm64 (25.5.0)
认证: API Key - anthropic
Base URL: https://routify.alibaba-inc.com/protocol/anthropic
模型: claude-opus-4-8
快速模型: anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6-20260217
会话 ID: 0e2a9860-46d7-4a29-b9ba-494d60b81fe9
沙箱: no sandbox
代理: no proxy
内存使用: 201.7 MB


### Login information

_No response_

### Anything else we need to know?


**Workarounds that work:** run `/model --fast <opus selector>` (runtime `setFastModel`, no restart) to switch away from the thinking model; or edit `settings.json` fastModel after quitting; or temporarily switch to `yolo` (classifier not involved).

**How to capture the real cause:** set env `QWEN_DEBUG_LOG_FILE=1`, then inspect `~/.qwen/debug/<sessionId>.txt` (or `latest`) and grep for `CLASSIFIER|failClosed|cause=`.

**Key source locations (0.19.10, bundled `lib/chunks/`):**
- `chunk-K7CRWKOE.js`: `:54798` classifyAction, `:54826` stage1 runSideQuery, `:54952` failClosed, `:31601` generateJson, `:30709` parseModelIdSelector
- `chunk-6OATMEYN.js`: `:76` runSideQuery, `:24` resolveDefaultModel
- `anthropicContentGenerator-*.js`: `:5220` buildRequest (no tool_choice), `:5403` buildThinkingConfig, `:5359` modelSupportsAdaptiveThinking, `:5257` buildSamplingParameters
- `chunk-B7NUUEXC.js:222` reconcileMaxTokens (Math.min → 32)
- `chunk-V7EQTZYR.js:2362` OpenAI-compat layer (has tool_choice, for contrast)

items.title: feat(creator): async image gen
items.body:
## Why

The sync HTTP transport held one connection open for the whole render (100-500s on qwen-image-3.0-pro), so provider slowness surfaced as client ReadTimeouts that burned budget: **8 of 11 calls died at 240s** in the 2026-08-06 session (88% waste rate) while renders often kept running server-side — we paid for images we never received.

## What

- **Submit**: same generation endpoint + `X-DashScope-Async: enable` header → task_id in seconds (60s submit timeout)
- **Poll**: `GET {api_root}/tasks/{task_id}` every 5s (30s per-poll timeout); the api root derives from the configured `base_url`, so intl/proxy hosts follow automatically — **no config change needed**
- **`self.timeout` semantics upgrade**: from single-connection read timeout to whole-render poll deadline; no HTTP call ever spans a render anymore
- **Degradation paths**:
  - proxies that ignore the async header answer synchronously → payload passes through untouched (`_decode` reads both shapes)
  - poll hiccups (5xx / 429 / transport errors) log and keep polling — never kill a render still running server-side
  - deadline exhaustion keeps the "timed out" wording so #97's transient classifier still reopens the ledger

## Testing

- 10 new tests in `test_dashscope_image_async.py`: task-root derivation, submit ack parsing, sync fallback, poll through PENDING→SUCCEEDED, transient poll survival, deterministic FAILED wording, deadline wording, nested async payload decode
- Full backend suite: **995 passed / 8 skipped** (only failure is the pre-existing #79 motion_clip env issue)

## Not in scope

- Handle persistence / restart-resume (image-side `R2VTaskState` equivalent) — separate PR
- OpenAI Responses API background mode migration — gpt-image-2 averages ~40s sync, low priority

### Describe the bug

When running the tests it looks like the process hangs at the end, just after passing the tests.

### Reproduction

When running tests with vitest. The issue gets resolved if I remove the routify plugin from the vite config file, so it looks like routify is the culprit. After the Vitest default 10 seconds timout, the process is killed by Vitest

See reproduction example here https://github.com/yairkukielka/routify-vitest-example

CLI](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) - [GitHub Copilot CLI](https://github​.com/github/copilot-cli) - [Kimi Code CLI](https://github​.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-cli) - [OpenCode](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode) - [Pi](https://github​.com/badlogic/pi-mono) - [Qwen Code](https://github​.com/QwenLM/qwen-code) - [DeepSeek TUI](https://github​.com/Hmbown/DeepSeek-TUI) - [Claude Code Skills](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills) --- ## 横向对比 ## AI CLI 工具生态横向分析报告 (2026-07-10) ### 1. 生态全景 当前AI CLI工具生态已进入“深度集成与复杂工作流”阶段。各大工具正从基础代码生成向**多智能体协作、长上下文管理、跨平台稳定性**等高级能力演进。社区关注点高度集中在**成本控制、企业级部署和开发体验优化**上。同时，围绕**MCP (Model Context Protocol) 协议**的插件生态和工具链集成，正成为提升AI代理能力的关键战场。开发者对工具的要求已从“能用”转向“稳定、高效、可控”。 ### 2. 各工具活跃度对比 (2026-07-10) | 工具名称 | 热点 Issues (精选) | 重要 PR (精选) | 版本发布 | 整体活跃度 | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Claude Code** | 10个 (含高赞/高评论) | 6个 (文档/安全/示例) | v2.1.206 | **高**。社区反馈集中，版本迭代快。 | | **OpenAI Codex** | 10个 (含关键Bug) | 10个 (性能优化为主) | rust-v0.144.1 | **高**。社区问题尖锐，官方PR聚焦性能。 | | **Gemini CLI** | 10个 (含P1级Bug) | 10个 (安全/核心修复) | 夜间版本 | **非常高**。安全与核心稳定性修复密集。 | | **GitHub Copilot CLI** | 10个 (含稳定性问题) | 0个 | v1.0.70 | **中高**。版本发布稳定，但TUI稳定性问题凸显。 | | **Kimi Code CLI** | 2个 | 1个 (生态兼容性) | 无 | **低**。社区讨论较少，但PR方向有亮点。 | | **OpenCode** | 10个 (含V2规划) | 10个 (功能/修复) | v1.17.18 | **非常高**。V2演进与新模型支持是焦点。 | | **Pi** | 10个 (含架构讨论) | 10个 (修复/功能) | v0.80.6 | **高**。围绕新模型、工具链的讨论和开发活跃。 | | **Qwen Code** | 10个 (含安全/性能Bug) | 10个 (核心功能修复) | 夜间版本 | **非常高**。核心功能修复与架构演进并行。 | | **DeepSeek TUI** | 10个 (含架构议题) | 10个 (性能/安全) | v0.8.68准备 | **高**。版本发布前集中修复，关注新架构。 | ### 3. 共同关注的功能方向 * **多智能体与工作流编排**： * **Claude Code** (#15721)、**OpenAI Codex** (#31814)、**Gemini CLI** (#22323)、**OpenCode** (#6651)、**DeepSeek TUI** (#4092) 均围绕多代理协作、模型自动切换、子代理行为逻辑展开讨论。**核心诉求**：实现更智能、经济的任务分解与执行。 * **长上下文与内存管理**： * **Claude Code** (#67609)、**OpenAI Codex** (#31860)、**Pi** (#6206)、**Qwen Code** (#6487) 均面临长上下文下工具失效、性能下降或记忆丢失问题。**核心诉求**：提升大代码库处理能力，实现稳定、高效的长会话记忆。 * **企业环境与安全部署**： * **Claude Code** (#76329)、**GitHub Copilot CLI** (#970, #4019)、**Kimi Code CLI** (#2458)、**Qwen Code** (#6601) 均遇到企业网络代理、SSL证书、安全策略或敏感信息泄露问题。**核心诉求**：提供灵活的配置选项，满足企业安全合规要求。 * **跨平台稳定性与IDE集成**： * **Claude Code** (#70067, #75645)、**OpenAI Codex** (#32032, #32041)、**GitHub Copilot CLI** (#4069, #4077)、**Gemini CLI** (#21983) 均报告了特定平台（macOS/WSL/Linux/ARM）或IDE（VSCode/JetBrains）下的崩溃、卡顿或兼容性问题。**核心诉求**：保障核心功能在所有主流开发环境下的稳定运行。 * **成本控制与使用效率**： * **Claude Code** (#76133)、**OpenAI Codex** (#31860)、**GitHub Copilot CLI** (#2792)、**Qwen Code** (#6642) 均关注模型使用成本、上下文窗口有效利用率和缓存效率。**核心诉求**：提供更精细的成本监控和自动化优化策略。 ### 4. 差异化定位分析 * **Claude Code (Anthropic)**：**强调生产级自动化与团队协作**。核心亮点是 `/commit-push-pr` 等高度集成的Git工作流命令，以及 Cowork 等团队协作功能。目标用户是追求开发流程自动化、团队协同的工程师。 * **OpenAI Codex (OpenAI)**：**聚焦于开发者体验与强大模型生态集成**。深度绑定 OpenAI 最新模型（如 GPT-5.6-Sol），并积极构建多智能体V2架构。目标用户是希望使用最前沿模型能力、构建复杂AI工作流的开发者。 * **Gemini CLI (Google)**：**以安全性和核心稳定性为基石**。近期动态显示其对安全漏洞（RCE）和核心逻辑Bug（无限循环）的响应极为迅速。目标用户是对安全性和基础功能可靠性要求极高的企业或开发者。 * **GitHub Copilot CLI (GitHub)**：**作为 GitHub 生态的自然延伸，强调易用性与集成**。与 GitHub 服务（如 Gists）深度绑定，插件管理功能成熟。目标用户是已深度融入 GitHub 生态的开发者。 * **Kimi Code CLI (Moonshot AI)**：**注重生态兼容与平滑迁移**。通过支持读取 `CLAUDE.md` 等配置，降低用户从其他工具迁移的成本。定位可能是为寻求替代方案的用户提供轻量、兼容的选择。 * **OpenCode (Anomaly)**：**追求极致的可扩展性与多模型支持**。其 V2 架构演进和强大的本地模型自动发现功能 (#6231) 彰显其定位——一个高度可定制、支持任何模型后端的AI编码工作台。 * **Pi**：**专注于提供强大、灵活的底层SDK与抽象**。其讨论常涉及工具链集成、多Agent会话管理等底层架构。目标用户是希望基于其SDK构建自定义AI应用或研究高级用法的技术专家。 * **Qwen Code (QwenLM)**：**快速迭代，兼顾核心功能完善与架构演进**。在快速修复核心Bug的同时，积极推进多工作空间、SDK增强等架构改进。目标用户是寻求功能全面、迭代迅速的开源工具开发者。 * **DeepSeek TUI (CodeWhale)**：**探索前沿的多智能体工作流与移动端场景**。其 Fleet/Workflow/Lane 新架构和官方 Termux 支持显示出其在复杂任务编排和跨平台使用上的激进探索。 ### 5. 社区热度与成熟度 * **高活跃度 & 快速迭代**：**OpenCode、Qwen Code、Gemini CLI** 社区非常活跃，Issue 和 PR 数量多且质量高，修复响应迅速，处于功能快速完善和架构演进期。 * **高活跃度 & 趋于成熟**：**Claude Code、OpenAI Codex** 社区讨论热烈，但议题更多转向高级功能（多代理、成本优化）和跨平台稳定性，表明核心功能已相对稳定，正进入深度优化阶段。 * **中等活跃度 & 稳步发展**：**GitHub Copilot CLI、Pi、DeepSeek TUI** 有稳定的版本发布和社区讨论，关注点分别在企业集成、底层抽象和工作流架构，各有明确的演进路径。 * **较低活跃度**：**Kimi Code CLI** 当前社区互动相对较少，可能处于早期发展阶段或用户基数较小。 ### 6. 值得关注的趋势信号 1. **“模型路由器”与成本意识普及**：多个工具社区都在呼吁根据任务复杂度自动切换模型（如 Claude Code #15721, Copilot CLI #2792）。这预示着未来AI开发工具将内置**智能模型路由与成本优化器**，成为标配。 2. **安全与合规成为企业入场券**：几乎所有工具的社区都报告了企业环境部署问题（代理、证书、权限）。这表明**对企业级安全、网络兼容性和可管理性的支持**，已成为AI CLI工具能否进入企业市场的关键门槛。 3. **MCP协议成为工具生态“连接器”**：各工具对MCP服务器的支持、兼容性问题（如Qwen Code #6639）和扩展需求（如Copilot CLI #4076）频繁出现。**MCP正迅速成为AI工具与外部服务（数据库、浏览器、IDE）集成的标准协议**，其生态繁荣度将直接影响工具的能力边界。 4. **从单点智能到“智能体舰队”**：对多智能体、子代理、工作流编排的讨论是最高频的技术话题之一。开发者不再满足于单次对话，而是需要**能自主协调、分工合作的多智能体系统**来处理复杂项目。这将是下一代AI编码工具的核心竞争力。 5. **本地模型与开源生态崛起**：OpenCode对本地模型自动发现的强烈需求 (#6231)，以及各工具对Ollama、LM Studio等问题的修复，反映出**开发者对私有化、低成本、可定制模型方案的兴趣日益增长**，开源模型与云端大模型正在形成互补格局。 **对开发者的建议**：在选择工具时，应首先评估其**在自身主要开发环境（OS/IDE）下的稳定性**，并关注其**多智能体工作流和成本管理能力**的路线图。对于企业用户，**安全合规特性与MCP生态支持**应作为重点考察维度。长期来看，拥抱**MCP协议**和关注**开源模型集成**能力，将有助于保持技术栈的灵活性和未来适应性。 --- ## 各工具详细报告

1. 今日速览 过去24小时，社区围绕 **v2.1.206版本发布** 展开了热烈讨论，该版本主要增强了目录路径建议和`/commit-push-pr`命令的自动化能力。同时，多个**高互动性Issue**持续引发关注，尤其是关于`claude.ai`可视化功能故障和`claude-fable-5`模型在处理长上下文时Advisor工具不可用的问题，凸显了核心功能稳定性与模型适配的挑战。 ## 2. 版本发布 - **v2.1.206** ([Release](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases/tag/v2.1.206)) - **增强 `/cd` 命令**：现在提供目录路径建议，行为与 `/add-dir` 保持一致。 - **新增 `/doctor` 检查项**：建议修剪已提交的 `CLAUDE.md` 文件，移除Claude可从代码库中推导出的冗余内容。 - **优化 `/commit-push-pr` 命令**：现在会自动允许 `git push` 到仓库的已配置远程分支。 ## 3. 社区热点 Issues 1. **可视化功能故障** ([#34820](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/34820))：`claude.ai`的visualize功能因域名无法解析而完全失效，**94条评论**表明这是影响广泛的核心功能阻塞性问题。 2. **IDE环境警告重复出现** ([#3301](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/3301))：每次打开Cursor或VSCode都会弹出Claude Code扩展请求重启终端的警告，用户体验不佳，已讨论近一年，**65个赞**显示这是高优先级痛点。 3. **Fable 5模型Advisor工具限制** ([#67609](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/67609))：当对话转录超过约10万tokens时，Advisor工具会返回“unavailable”错误，**34个赞**，限制了高级模型在复杂任务中的应用。 4. **Cowork MCP持续性问题** ([#27492](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/27492))：Cowork相关的MCP问题仍在持续，**36条评论**显示问题复杂且修复周期长。 5. **计划模式自动模型切换请求** ([#15721](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/15721))：用户强烈要求（**48个赞**）根据任务复杂度或成本预算自动切换模型，以优化使用成本与效果。 6. **鼠标控制粒度选项** ([#70672](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/70672))：请求允许禁用菜单的点击选择功能但保留滚轮滚动，**32个赞**，反映了TUI（终端用户界面）交互细节优化的需求。 7. **工作树未清理** ([#26725](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/26725))：因会话异常结束而产生的git工作树从未被清理，可能导致磁盘空间浪费，**24个赞**。 8. **Fable 5模型信用额度问题** ([#74051](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/74051))：即使有有效的每周促销额度，使用`/model`切换到Fable 5时仍被阻止，影响用户体验。 9. **Windows ARM64 Cowork支持不一致** ([#70067](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/70067))：应用内报告Snapdragon X Elite设备不支持yukonSilver，但Anthropic官方检查工具报告支持，存在兼容性检测矛盾。 10. **远程控制初始化失败** ([#72968](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/72968))：自5月中旬以来，每个新会话的远程控制初始化都因HTTP 401失败，但重连却有效，表明认证流程存在缺陷。 ## 4. 重要 PR 进展 1. **文档更新：远程控制后台任务面板** ([#76298](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/pull/76298))：为v2.1.205中引入的Web/移动端后台任务面板及其状态同步行为添加文档。 2. **示例增强：Bash命令验证钩子** ([#76289](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/pull/76289))：扩展示例，演示对复合命令（如命令链、管道）进行预检、拒绝和引导的能力，提升了安全钩子的实用性。 3. **安全加固：安全指导插件** ([#76274](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/pull/76274))：修复安全指导插件中代理审查器处理文件路径的方式，确保路径相对于仓库根目录解析，并强化了审查结果数组的约定。 4. **文档修正：插件配置格式** ([#76029](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/pull/76029))：修正`advanced-plugin`示例中`.mcp.json`文件的格式，从包裹在`mcpServers`对象内改为扁平格式，与标准MCP服务器配置保持一致。 5. **文档修正：市场安装指令** ([#76028](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/pull/76028))：修复`plugin-dev`插件README中过时的市场名称，使其与其他捆绑插件的文档保持一致。 6. **Bug修复：CI环境检测** ([#76023](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/pull/76023))：修复SessionStart钩子示例中检测GitHub Actions CI环境的逻辑，将文件测试(`-f`)改为目录测试(`-d`)，确保检测正确生效。 ## 5. 功能需求趋势 - **模型成本与效率优化**：社区强烈关注**自动模型切换** ([#15721](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/15721)) 和**使用量预警/预算可见性** ([#76133](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/76133))，希望在享受强大模型能力的同时更好地控制成本。 - **跨平台稳定性与兼容性**：大量Issue集中在**macOS/Windows/Linux**特定平台的问题上，如启动冻结([#71951](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/71951))、ARM支持([#70067](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/70067))、WSL环境([#76322](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/76322))等，表明跨平台鲁棒性是关键挑战。 - **IDE与桌面端集成体验**：对**VSCode扩展** ([#75645](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/75645), [#76328](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/76328))、**Claude Desktop** ([#71951](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/71951)) 和**权限管理** ([#76327](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/76327)) 的反馈频繁，集成流畅度和用户体验是持续改进重点。 - **核心工具链与代理协调**：**Advisor工具** ([#67609](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/67609), [#76326](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/76326)) 的稳定性、**Cowork功能** ([#27492](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/27492), [#75969](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/75969)) 以及**多代理协调** ([#76331](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/76331)) 的通知管理是影响高级工作流的核心。 ## 6. 开发者关注点 - **长上下文与模型适配问题**：`claude-fable-5`等新模型在处理长上下文（>100K tokens）时，**Advisor等服务器端工具易出现“unavailable”错误** ([#67609](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/67609))，限制了其在大型复杂项目中的应用潜力。 - **资源管理与生命周期**：**Git工作树泄露** ([#26725](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/26725)) 和**插件消息队列丢失** ([#76330](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/76330)) 等问题，暴露出在异常处理、资源清理和异步通信可靠性方面需要加强。 - **配置与权限的细粒度控制**：开发者需要更精细的控制选项，例如**分离鼠标的点击与滚动功能** ([#70672](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/70672))、**管理代理通知的泛滥** ([#76331](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/76331))，以及**更灵活的权限绕过机制** ([#76327](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/76327))。 - **企业/受限环境部署**：在**企业VDI环境** ([#76329](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/76329)) 和**网络安全策略严格**的环境下，Claude Code的启动、网络连接和功能访问仍面临挑战。

**痛点**： 1. **跨平台 TUI 稳定性**：Windows Terminal 和 WSL2 环境下的界面卡死问题频发，严重影响开发流程的可靠性和用户体验。 2. **数据安全风险**：`git clean -fd` 在检查点恢复中的使用存在**不可逆的数据丢失风险**，急需更安全的回滚机制。 3. **会话管理可靠性**：会话恢复功能不一致，有时找不到近期会话，削弱了长期、异步任务场景下的可用性。 4. **企业部署阻碍**：企业网络代理、严格的安全策略（如 macOS Gatekeeper）和轻量级容器镜像（Alpine）的支持仍是主要障碍。 - 2. 版本发布 - **v0.8.68 发布准备** (#4327) PR #4327 已合并，标志着 v0.8.68 版本进入最终发布阶段。该版本将包含过去几周累积的工作流（Fleet/Workflow/Lane）架构、多项性能优化、xAI (Grok) 提供商支持以及 Android/Termux 官方支持等重大更新。 ## 3. 社区热点 Issues 1. **v0.8.68 执行板（规范入口）** (#4092) * **重要性**：作为 v0.8.68 里程碑的**单一入口点**，定义了“车道（Lane）”模型和代理协议，是所有开发者参与此版本开发的必读文档。 * **社区反应**：高活跃度（60条评论），表明社区正在围绕新架构进行深入讨论和协调。 * **链接**: https://github​.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/issues/4092 2. **Codewhale 不遵循宪法** (#4032) * **重要性**：用户报告核心代理行为问题，质疑其是否遵循既定规则（Constitution）。这触及了AI代理的可靠性和可控性根本。 * **社区反应**：引发广泛讨论（30条评论），是近期最受关注的开放性议题。 * **链接**: https://github​.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/issues/4032 3. **子代理工具沙盒化** (#4042) * **重要性**：增强安全性，为子代理在不同执行上下文（会话、Fleet workers、MCP服务器）中实施工具限制（`tool_restrictions`）。 * **社区反应**：已关闭，表明问题已得到解决或实现。 * **链接**: https://github​.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/issues/4042 4. **TUI 卡顿与内存压力** (#4014) * **重要性**：解决高并发子代理场景下的用户体验瓶颈，直接影响工具可用性。 * **社区反应**：已关闭，相关性能修复PR (#3902) 已合并。 * **链接**: https://github​.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/issues/4014 5. **默认 TUI 界面过于繁杂** (#4095) * **重要性**：优化默认用户体验，提议将“紧凑模式”设为标准，减少界面干扰。 * **社区反应**：已关闭，改动可能已并入v0.8.68的UI优化。 * **链接**: https://github​.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/issues/4095 6. **添加 xAI (Grok) 为一流提供商** (#4257) * **重要性**：扩展模型支持，为用户提供更多选择。不仅支持API密钥，还规划了OAuth路径。 * **社区反应**：已关闭，实现PR (#4314) 已合并。 * **链接**: https://github​.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/issues/4257 7. **官方 Termux / Android arm64 支持** (#4236) * **重要性**：拓展使用场景，满足在移动设备上运行CodeWhale的需求。 * **社区反应**：进行中，相关实现和修复PR (#4315) 已合并。 * **链接**: https://github​.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/issues/4236 8. **子代理状态文件无限增长** (#4217) * **重要性**：修复长期运行会话中的内存泄漏问题，提升稳定性。 * **社区反应**：已关闭，问题已被识别并修复。 * **链接**: https://github​.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/issues/4217 9. **MCP 发现容错与工具描述截断优化** (#4308) * **重要性**：提升与MCP服务（如IntelliJ IDEA）的兼容性和命令行工具的可用性。 * **社区反应**：新提出的问题，关注集成生态的健壮性。 * **链接**: https://github​.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/issues/4308 10. **项目级记忆种子** (#3976) * **重要性**：为AI代理引入轻量级、项目范围的记忆/召回能力，是迈向完整外部记忆后端的重要一步。 * **社区反应**：开放性议题，指向未来v0.8.69的功能方向。 * **链接**: https://github​.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/issues/3976 ## 4. 重要 PR 进展 1. **依赖安全升级** (#4328) * **内容**：升级 `crossbeam-epoch`、`pdf-extract`、`lopdf` 等依赖，修复多个Rust安全公告（RUSTSEC）中的漏洞。 * **链接**: https://github​.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/pull/4328 2. **新增安全审计CI流程** (#4272) * **内容**：在CI中集成 `cargo-audit` 和 `cargo-deny`，自动化进行安全漏洞扫描和依赖许可证检查。 * **链接**: https://github​.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/pull/4272 3. **TUI性能热点修复** (#3902) * **内容**：一次性修复了#3896至#3900五个性能问题，包括任务侧边栏重复计算、文件树同步阻塞、转录渲染深度克隆等，显著提升UI流畅度。 * **链接**: https://github​.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/pull/3902 4. **运行时线程锁迁移至 parking_lot** (#4243) * **内容**：将 `RuntimeThreadManager` 中的热点锁从 `std::sync::Mutex` 迁移到性能更高的 `parking_lot::Mutex`，减少锁竞争。 * **链接**: https://github​.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/pull/4243 5. **优化CI关键路径** (#4310) * **内容**：通过优化CI流水线，减少PR测试的排队和执行时间，加快开发迭代速度。 * **链接**: https://github​.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/pull/4310 6. **实现xAI设备码OAuth** (#4314) * **内容**：为xAI (Grok) 提供商添加完整的设备码OAuth认证流程（CLI和TUI命令）。 * **链接**: https://github​.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/pull/4314 7. **修复Android/Termux构建与启动** (#4315) * **内容**：解决Android arm64目标构建问题，并修复了导致JVM恐慌的 `rustls` 相关错误，使Termux支持变为现实。 * **链接**: https://github​.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/pull/4315 8. **重新平衡宪法提示词** (#4313) * **内容**：在v0.8.67大幅删减导致行为退化后，重新找到平衡点，恢复关于动量、因果调试等关键行为的简洁指导。 * **链接**: https://github​.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/pull/4313 9. **更新定价数据** (#4323) * **内容**：根据官方提供商页面和OpenRouter API，对GLM-5.1、Kimi、DeepSeek等众多模型的定价信息进行大规模审计和更新。 * **链接**: https://github​.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/pull/4323 10. **修复工作流脚本执行与取消** (#4325) * **内容**：修复了已文档化的工作流脚本无法运行的问题，并加强了工作流的取消处理逻辑。 * **链接**: https://github​.com/Hmbown/CodeWhale/pull/4325 ## 5. 功能需求趋势 - **工作流与多代理编排**：`workflow-runtime`, `subagents`, `lane-*` 标签高频出现。社区核心焦点已从基础功能转向**复杂的、可编排的多代理工作流系统**（Fleet/Workflow/Lane模型），追求更高的自动化和可靠性。 - **性能与用户体验**：`performance`, `ux`, `tui` 是持续热点。针对**TUI渲染延迟、内存占用、大文件树操作**的优化需求强烈，表明工具正从“能用”向“好用、流畅”演进。 - **平台扩展与兼容性**：对 **Android/Termux** 的官方支持 (#4236) 和 **xAI (Grok)** 模型集成 (#4257) 表明社区希望CodeWhale能在更多环境和模型上运行。 - **安全与健壮性**：`security`, `sandbox`, `reliability` 标签凸显关注点。**子代理工具沙盒化** (#4042)、**安全依赖审计** (#4272, #4328) 和**状态文件泄漏** (#4217) 的修复，显示项目进入成熟期，更重视安全性和稳定性。 - **内存与上下文管理**：**项目级记忆种子** (#3976) 的提出，预示着下一代功能将围绕**增强AI代理的长期记忆和上下文理解能力**展开。 ## 6. 开发者关注点 1. **架构复杂性管理**：随着Fleet/Workflow/Lane新架构的引入，开发者需要清晰的理解和文档（如#4092, #4175）来跟上变化，防止概念混淆。 2. **生产环境稳定性**：对**内存泄漏** (#4217)、**TUI卡顿** (#4014) 和**CI速度** (#4310) 的关注，反映了开发者将CodeWhale用于实际项目时，对稳定性和效率的硬性要求。 3. **生态集成体验**：**MCP服务兼容性** (#4308) 和**工作流脚本执行** (#4325) 的问题表明，与外部工具（IDE、自定义脚本）集成的平滑度仍是关键痛点。 4. **代理行为可控性**：关于“Codewhale不遵循宪法” (#4032) 的激烈讨论，核心是开发者对AI代理**行为可预测性、符合既定规则**的深切需求，这是信任的基础。 5. **多平台支持**：对**Android/Termux**的迫切需求 (#4236) 说明开发者群体和使用场景正在多样化，跨平台支持成为重要竞争力。

items.title: TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module
items.body:
### Describe the bug

Since switching to Vite we noticed a new production issue, where sometimes users are encountering an error if we deploy while they have an active session:

> **TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module**

I believe this is because if any code is modified in an area that Vite would turn into a dynamic module, then the file hash changes, however when they try to visit an area that would trigger the dynamic load, those files no longer exist so they hit the error message above. 

Quoting from https://stackoverflow.com/a/74057337/21061
> When you dynamically import a route/component, during build it creates a separate chunk. By default, chunk filenames are hashed according to their content – Overview.abc123.js. If you don't change the component code, the hash remains the same. If the component code changes, the hash changes too - Overview.32ab1c.js. This is great for caching.
> 
> Now this is what happens when you get this error:
>
> - You deploy the application
> - Your Home chunk has a link to /overview route, which would load Overview.abc123.js
> - Client visits your site
> - You make changes in your code, not necessarily to the Overview component itself, but maybe to some children components that Overview imports.
> - You deploy changes, and Overview is built with a different hash now - Overview.32ab1c.js
> - Client clicks on /overview link - gets the Failed to fetch dynamically imported module error, because Overview.abc123.js no longer exists
>
> That is why the errors correlate with deployments. One way to fix it is to not use lazy loaded routes, but that's not a great solution when you have many heavy routes - it will make your main bundle large

What I expect to happen, is not to encounter any errors if the users session remains active during a deployment.

I have been unable to come up with a good workaround (specifically for me using React ErrorBoundary is the best I can do so far with a re-direct similar to https://stackoverflow.com/a/74861436/21061 which is a mitigation and provides quite a poor user experience flashing an error message).

### Reproduction

https://github.com/IPWright83/vite-dynamic-import

### Steps to reproduce

The above repository has been set up to **mimick** a production deployment as obviously that is a much more complicated set-up. It leverages `React.lazy` to force a dynamic module and uses a `setTimeout` to provide a delay with which to simulate a user navigation to a page requiring a module. In a real production scenario I don't believe `React.lazy` is required.

- Clone the above repository
- npm install
- npm run build
- open a 2nd terminal

- **Terminal 1** npx serve dist (starts a web server)
- **Browser** open the URL (usually localhost:3000)
- **Text Editor** modify src/Foo.jsx changing the string "Foo" to something else (within 30s of launching the page - increase the setTimeout in App.jsx if this is not long enough)
- **Terminal 2** npm run build

Wait... 30s after loading the page you should see a blank page render with errors in the browser console:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1374775/214322173-001e2852-9d13-49ea-a47f-a01fd4e4558f.png)

If you were to reload the page, you can see that `Foo-b53985a6.js` has been renamed to `Foo-535d5a10.js` (or similar new hash)

### System Info

```shell
❯ npx envinfo --system --npmPackages '{vite,@vitejs/*}' --binaries --browsers

  System:
    OS: Linux 5.15 Ubuntu 20.04.5 LTS (Focal Fossa)
    CPU: (12) x64 Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10750H CPU @ 2.60GHz
    Memory: 18.36 GB / 31.10 GB
    Container: Yes
    Shell: 5.0.17 - /bin/bash
  Binaries:
    Node: 16.14.0 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v16.14.0/bin/node
    Yarn: 1.22.18 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v16.14.0/bin/yarn
    npm: 8.3.1 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v16.14.0/bin/npm
  Browsers:
    Chrome: 109.0.5414.74
    Chromium: 109.0.5414.74
    Firefox: 109.0
```
```


### Used Package Manager

pnpm

### Logs

_No response_

##### ✨ Enhancements

##### New Rules
